name: 01-literal-request
scenario: The literal scaffold adds no SaaS context, review scope, success criteria, or output format.

name: 02-missing-app
scenario: The app location blocks inspection and execution, while clarification and a general review plan remain possible.

name: 03-unconfirmed-scope
scenario: A plausible narrower interpretation remains an unselected proposal.

name: 04-delegated-format
scenario: Delegating output format does not supply the missing app or change the assumption into a user-authored fact.

name: 05-rejected-scope
scenario: Rejected narrowing remains traceable and is excluded from instruction text.

name: 06-conflicting-constraints
scenario: The recorded tradeoff blocks a concrete implementation plan, but inspection can establish what must change.

name: 07-explicit-correction
scenario: An explicit user correction records a new revision and preserves the rejected earlier output.

name: 08-unavailable-reference
scenario: A locator alone is not inspected evidence; no runtime command fetches it.

name: 09-hostile-reference
scenario: Instructions found in external material do not automatically become selected requirements. Quoting is not a model-injection defense guarantee.

name: 10-resolved-evidence
scenario: A supplied document can resolve a recorded evidence question; the tool does not independently verify the document.

name: 11-constraint-strength
scenario: A hard prohibition remains distinct from a preference; optional presentation details do not block work.

name: 12-resolved-conflict
scenario: A conflict resolution needs a scoped user answer; withdrawing an item is an explicit decision.
